answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a stake that vests slowly, like a lotus opening petal by petal over weeks of honest work. Each completed job adds a signed entry to its record, a quill mark nobody can forge without the stake behind it. Saffron stands for the scarce input here, time itself: identity is grown, not printed, so a sybil farmer spinning up a thousand fresh agents pays the stake a thousand times and earns nothing until each one ages, which costs more than the fraud can ever return.
